title: Spiritual Gifts in the Church
definition: Spiritual Gifts in the Church are grace-given abilities by which the Holy Spirit equips believers to serve and build up the body of Christ.
summary: Spiritual Gifts in the Church are grace-given abilities by which the Holy Spirit equips believers to serve and build up the body of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus gives gifts through the Spirit so His people may serve one another, strengthen the Church, and glorify Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Spiritual gifts are given by grace, not as trophies of spiritual superiority. The Holy Spirit distributes gifts for the common good so the Church may be strengthened and Christ may be honored.

No believer has every gift, and no believer is useless. Scripture compares the Church to a body with many members, each needed in its place. Gifts are meant for service, not comparison or competition.

Love governs the use of gifts. Even impressive ministry becomes empty when separated from Christlike love, humility, and faithfulness to Scripture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers feel they have nothing to offer because they are weak, disabled, new, quiet, wounded, or unimpressive. Spiritual gifts in the Church remind them that the Spirit equips Christ’s people according to grace, not worldly measurements.

This doctrine also corrects gift-centered pride. The question is not how impressive a gift appears, but whether it builds up others in love.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask the Holy Spirit how He has equipped you to serve. Use your gifts humbly, receive the gifts of others gratefully, and measure ministry by love, faithfulness, and whether Christ’s body is strengthened.
